summary.text: Jeff Van Drew is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 2nd District. A dentist by training, he held local office in Dennis Township and Cape May County and served in the New Jersey Legislature before winning Congress as a Democrat in 2018; in December 2019 he switched to the Republican Party. He sits on the House Judiciary and Transportation and Infrastructure Committees.

paragraphs.text: Van Drew was born in New York City on February 23, 1953.
He earned a B.S. from Rutgers University and, according to his House biography, a D.M.D. degree from Fairleigh Dickinson University.

He worked as a dentist, and his House biography says he owned and operated a dental practice in South Jersey for 30 years; Wikipedia reports he has served as president of the New Jersey Dental Society.

Van Drew's public service began in Cape May County, where, according to Wikipedia, he was a Dennis Township fire commissioner (1983-1986), a township committee member (1991) and a Cape May County freeholder (1994-1997 and 2000-2002).
He was mayor of Dennis Township in 1994-1995 and 1997-2003.
He then served in the New Jersey General Assembly (2002-2007) and the State Senate (2008-2019); his House biography counts three Assembly terms and four Senate terms.
In November 2018 Van Drew won the open 2nd District seat as a Democrat, defeating Republican Seth Grossman 52.9% to 45.2% after Rep. Frank LoBiondo announced his retirement.
On December 19, 2019, a day after voting against both articles of impeachment against President Trump, he announced he was switching from the Democratic to the Republican Party.
He was re-elected in 2020, 2022 and 2024; his House biography describes the 2024 win as his fourth term and says he was sworn in on January 3, 2025.
Van Drew serves on the House Judiciary Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.
According to his House biography, he and his wife have two children and two grandchildren and live in Dennis Township.
